allowed_use: Whether concurrently dispatched programs of a grouped matrix launch share an operand tile that they reference at the same K step, and the relative magnitude of that sharing across group widths. The comparison is between group widths at a fixed instruction stream, geometry and logical request volume.

derived_l2_served_fraction.definition: 1 - configured_dram_read_capability / probe_logical_byte_rate, valid while the probe is DRAM bound

finding: Both targets share operands between concurrently dispatched programs, but by very different amounts. Against each target's configured DRAM read capability (metax_c500 918.372 B/clk x 1.8 GHz = 1653 GB/s, nvidia_a800 1124 B/clk x 1.593 GHz = 1791 GB/s), the L2-served fraction of the probe's logical requests is: metax_c500 26.0 / 21.1 / 15.1 / 13.5 / 12.8 percent at group width 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16, and nvidia_a800 67.0 / 65.6 / 67.9 / 68.1 / 70.5 percent. A model in which the resident wave of programs advances through K together predicts 69.6 / 73.4 / 84.4 / 87.5 / 84.4 percent for this geometry. nvidia_a800 matches that model at group width 1 (67.0 measured against 69.6 predicted) and falls short only where the sharing needs many distinct objects co-resident. metax_c500 falls short everywhere, by 2.6x at group width 1. At that width the co-resident working set is about 528 KiB against a documented 8 MiB L2, so the shortfall is not a capacity effect; narrowing the resident-program window cannot reproduce it either, because that window floors the predicted served fraction near 49 percent for this geometry. The metax_c500 shortfall is therefore a property of how its L2 services this access structure, not of how many programs are concurrent.
forbidden_use: An absolute DRAM bandwidth, an L2 capacity, a production operator duration, or a per-shape traffic correction. The logical byte rate is a probe rate, not a hardware peak.

nvidia_a800_dram_counter_ground_truth.finding: With real counters the measured served fraction rises with group width, 57.7 to 75.5 percent, so the grouped swizzle does buy sharing on this target. The same-K-step sharing model over-credits it by a roughly uniform 9 to 14 points rather than by the 26 the retracted metric claimed. No metax_c500 counterpart exists yet; wall clock cannot substitute for it.

retraction: The wall-clock derived l2_served_fraction in this reference and in grouped_program_l2_service_knee.json is RETRACTED. It was computed as 1 - configured_dram_read_capability / logical_byte_rate, which is only valid if the probe is DRAM bound. A direct nvidia_a800 measurement with dram__bytes_read.sum and l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_bytes.sum shows the probe is not DRAM bound: at the same geometry the true served fraction is 57.7 / 60.9 / 71.7 / 73.2 / 75.5 percent at group width 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16, against 67.0 / 65.6 / 67.9 / 68.1 / 70.5 from the wall-clock expression. The wall-clock numbers are wrong in level everywhere and wrong in trend at the low widths. Every conclusion drawn from them is withdrawn, including the reported metax_c500 levels, the claim that the sharing model over-credits by 26 points, and the absence of a knee at 8 MiB. The raw timings are kept because they are correct measurements of the probe's duration; only the served-fraction interpretation fails. A usable version of this probe must either be made genuinely DRAM bound or read DRAM counters directly, which on metax_c500 means mcProfiler.
